messages:
melissa: Quick Q — we have a mid-year hire (start 7/1) who asked how PTO accrual and sick-day top-ups work when they join after the half-year blackout. Do we pro-rate carryover eligibility or apply an exception?
jordan: For accruals we pro-rate from start date, same as usual. Carryover eligibility is trickier — depends on blackout window dates. Which blackout period are you referring to?
melissa: The July 1–July 14 hiring cohort — last year's mid-year hiring freeze was June 15–July 7 but product put a short blackout this year 6/28–7/10 for major launches. Question is whether folks who start 7/1 inside that brief blackout get flagged as "new hire in blackout" and disallowed carryover.
samir: Short answer: we treat carryover eligibility on the employee's continuous service and hire date relative to calendar-year cutoff. Longer: policy excerpt below.
hr-bot: PASTE POLICY: 
```
Carryover eligibility: Employees employed on Dec 31 are eligible for carryover. New hires are eligible for pro-rated accruals beginning their first full pay period. Blackout windows for PTO usage do NOT automatically block carryover eligibility but may restrict taking PTO during the window. Exceptions can be granted by People Ops for operationally required hires.
```
melissa: That's helpful. Two follow-ups: 1) Does the "first full pay period" rule mean we count from 7/1 or from the first Monday after 7/1? 2) Sick-day top-ups — we have a small top-up pool for critical hires (6 days). Are those awarded automatically or via manager request?
jordan: Pay-period alignment: payroll runs biweekly starting Mondays, so if hire is mid-period we count pro-rated accruals for that partial period. So 7/1 mid-week => pro-rate that period.
peter: Sick top-ups: usually manager requests to People Ops with business justification. We don't auto-grant, but for roles hired into blackout rotations we approved a small auto-top-up (one-time) last year — need to confirm if that's still authorized.
melissa: Ok — can you confirm if we have an approved one-time auto-top-up for hires inside a launch blackout this cycle? If yes we'll communicate to hiring managers.
samir: I'll check records and loop legal if needed. If we want to automate, we should add a short checkbox in the hiring checklist: "Auto sick-top-up approved (Y/N)". @peter can you add to the hire-runbook?
peter: Yep, will add a checkbox and a note: "Manager must submit request to People Ops within 30 days for auto-top-up to be applied."
melissa: Great. Also will draft a short FAQ blurb: "Joining during a PTO blackout does not prevent carryover eligibility; accruals are pro-rated; sick top-ups require manager request unless explicitly granted via hire checklist." Will post here for review before publishing. :+1:
samir: Thanks — ping me the draft. If we decide to auto-grant again, we'll log the criteria in the policy doc and enable payroll tagging for the one-time grant.
melissa: Draft posted -> https://redwood.internal/people-ops/faq/ptoblackout-midyear (will update later). End."
